what: the molecular-opacity lever on the AGSS21 atomic N I set, measured PAIRED
design: same 4 lines, same code, same holding, same fitter. ONE variable: `use_molecules` on the red-optical band. Run from a SEPARATE checkout whose only diff from production is that flag, so the lever is the molecules and not code drift — measuring against the already-published atoms-only number would have measured both (the lesson of 'measure a lever paired, not against the feed').
result: -0.174 to -0.228 dex, and the four-line scatter collapses from 0.138-0.244 to 0.030-0.158. Adding real opacity made the lines AGREE, which is the signature of opacity that was genuinely missing rather than a fudge that happened to move the mean.
interpretation: ~40% of the +0.5 dex offset against AGSS21 is missing CN opacity. The remainder is atomic blend contamination: N I carries 0.9-5.9% of its own fit window against Fe 87%, Si 69%, Ti 88%. Molecules only partly fix a line that is a minority absorber in its own window.
consequence: the red-optical band's production config still declares use_molecules: false. Flipping it is a config change with a measured lever behind it, and it would move every red-optical CNO product — so it is REPORTED here and not done inside this ticket (RYA-832: a published number does not move without a stated cause).
